title: A small logging library
hints: Start without threads: the struct with the level, the counts and a ring of lines (`start` is the oldest line, `used` how many are stored). Get `logger_write` and `logger_history` right, then add the mutex around every touch of the shared fields.
A ring buffer: while it is not full, the next slot is `(start + used) % capacity`; once full, overwrite the slot at `start` and move `start` on by one.
Format the message into a local buffer with `vsnprintf` **before** taking the lock, so the slow formatting does not keep other threads waiting.
requirements: The history is a fixed ring buffer of lines inside one allocation (a flexible array member or a fixed array).
A mutex makes every function thread-safe, and cleanup frees everything.
`logger_history` behaves like `snprintf`: never overflows, always terminates, returns the full length.
stretch: A log file as a second destination, timestamps with `time` and `strftime`, and a `__attribute__((format(printf, 3, 4)))` on `logger_write` so the compiler checks the formats.
